(1) The version-skew claim in the ledger is wrong. It says the fix 'protects only against reverts done by a build carrying this fix, which is the build doing the reverting, so that is correct'. But the marker is WRITTEN by the fleeing build and READ only by the RESTORED build (_load_upgrade_state / _upgrade_attempt_blocked run in vX-1). So if the first release carrying this fix (0.9.78) crash-loops, revert_to_previous_build (upgrade.py:1077) restores 0.9.77. 0.9.77 has no crash_looped gate, and its own note_upgrade_attempt drops the unknown keys on a version change. It reinstalls 0.9.78 on its first report reply, which is exactly the finding's scenario. The companion fix only protects a machine once two consecutive builds carry it. The dashboard-side defence the ledger calls 'optional' is the only thing that covers the next release. Something must also persist it per machine, because upgrade_reverted_from is cleared after one accepted report (_note_report_accepted, app.py ~6676). The minimum is to stop pushing or auto-offering a version equal to the machine's last reported reverted_from. This should be an owed item, not optional.
(2) Nothing reports the block. crash_looped is not in upgrade_report (upgrade.py ~560), and reverted_from goes out once. A fresh admin re-push (new requested_at) is also refused silently and for ever, with nothing on the dashboard to explain it. Either send crash_looped in the sync_guard.upgrade block (a new optional key needs the dashboard to accept it first, which is the usual deploy order), or document it as owed.
Minor: only one fled version is remembered. A second revert (vX+1) overwrites crash_looped=vX. If an admin then makes vX current again, auto-update on vX-1 would take vX again (it is newer than the running build).

(1) server_files is not wired. The only caller, app.py:8225, passes no server_files, and the ledger's 'OWED' names no group. So on every machine, _split_folder_for_4b (file_moves.py ~497) has inventory None. Any 4b folder containing even one lane A original is kept WHOLE and answered ok=True with DETAIL_KEPT_LOCAL_ONLY. app.py ~8255 records that as a plain done move (state None). recent_excludes (file_moves.py ~1220) then drops the exclusion after EXCLUDE_WINDOW_SECONDS (24 h), because a done row is not in the unresolved set. Lane A then uploads every original in the folder back to the OLD server path. Who holds originals locally? Usually the machine that ingested and already uploaded them, so this is the common case, not the card-dump edge. Scenario: the owner drags a 300 GB Card_07 from project X into project Y. A day later every X-syncing machine that ingested it re-uploads the whole 300 GB to X/Card_07. The folder 'comes back', which is the exact failure docs/FILE_MOVES.md and CLAUDE.md say a move must never cause. The MOVES history shows the machine as done. HEAD risked losing unuploaded originals in a rare case. The fix guarantees a full duplicate re-upload in the ordinary case. Needed: wire server_files=file_moves_mod.rclone_server_files(<lane A rclone path, remote, remote_root>) at app.py:8225 in this wave. Failing that, make the no-listing fallback answer not-ok 'retrying' (keeping the RES-1 unresolved exclusion open, as the finding suggested) instead of ok/done.
(2) _held_by_server (file_moves.py ~478) is O(files x inventory), and it calls _cmp_key on every inventory entry for every local file. A card dump of several thousand clips means tens of millions of NFC normalisations on the report-command thread. Build a set of (_cmp_key(rel), size) once per split.
(3) _is_lane_a_original is given the rel UNDER the moved folder, not the full path. So a moved folder that is itself a Proxy dir, or sits under one, classifies its .mov/.mp4 proxies as originals and keeps them whole. That is the safe direction, but lane A will never upload them, so they sit at the old path for ever. Passing from_project_rel/from_rel + rel would match lane A's real classification.
rclone_server_files is unwired and only unit-tested with a stub run_fn. Its remote path composition (remote_root + 'Projects/' + dest) has not been checked against a live lane A run.
